response.justification: The candidate has notable geospatial (GISCollective) and distributed/high-performance systems experience (Sociomantic/Dunnhumby), but his core technical trajectory over the last decade has moved firmly toward TypeScript/Node.js full-stack and web development. His C/C++ experience is minimal, dated (mostly 2014-2015), and there is no evidence of Rust, navigation systems, or routing-tile production pipeline work, making him a weak match for a role centered on modern C++/Rust systems engineering.
strengths: Hands-on geospatial/GIS platform experience via GISCollective, including event-driven architecture and kubernetes deployment
Proven distributed systems and low-latency engineering background from Sociomantic (async I/O, fibers, high-throughput microservices)
Demonstrated adaptability across many languages/stacks and strong communication/teaching skills (talks, workshops)
concerns: Very limited and outdated C++ experience (roughly one year, ~2014-2015), not matching 'modern C++' expectations
No Rust experience at all, despite it being the stated alternative to C++
No direct navigation/routing system experience, and recent 4+ years focused on TypeScript/Node.js product work rather than systems-level programming

key_factors.factor: Lack of modern C++/Rust production experience
No navigation systems or routing-tile domain experience
